summary.text: John Olszewski Jr. is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 2nd Congressional District. A former Baltimore County public school teacher, he served in the Maryland House of Delegates and as Baltimore County Executive before being sworn into Congress in January 2025. He is seeking a second term.

paragraphs.text: Olszewski was born in Baltimore, Maryland, in 1982, and according to his congressional website he is a product of Maryland's public schools and a first-generation college graduate.

He earned a bachelor's degree from Goucher College in 2004, a master's degree from George Washington University in 2005, and a Ph.D. in public policy from the University of Maryland-Baltimore County in 2017.

He began his career as a teacher in the Baltimore County Public Schools system; Ballotpedia also lists work as a senior manager of legislative affairs for the City of Baltimore and as a software executive at SAS.
Olszewski served in the Maryland House of Delegates for more than nine years and, according to his congressional website, was the youngest lawmaker to chair Baltimore County's House delegation.
He was twice elected Baltimore County Executive, leading Maryland's third-largest jurisdiction, with a $5 billion budget and more than 9,000 employees.

His congressional website cites the county's near-universal free community college program, its first public campaign finance system, and an Office of the Inspector General among his administration's initiatives.
Olszewski was sworn into Congress in January 2025 and serves on the Small Business and Foreign Affairs Committees and on the Democratic Steering and Policy Committee.
He won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 84.5% of the vote over Clint Spellman Jr.
According to his congressional website, he lives in eastern Baltimore County with his wife, Marisa, and their daughter.
